methodology.title: How we work
methodology.metaDescription: How AIToolsWijzer decides the order, what our statuses mean, how we track how sure and how recent things are, and what our software checks automatically.
methodology.intro: Here you read how we decide the order and how we know what we know. This is also how we explain our rankings, as EU consumer law asks (Omnibus Directive).
methodology.rankingBody:
When you ask a question, our system picks the tool that fits best for each step of your task. This is what counts, most important first:

1. Fit: is this the tool's main feature, or can the tool do it too?
2. Your requirements: budget, level, data in the EU, language, where it works, watermark and open source. A hard requirement removes tools. Does nothing fit? Then we say so.
3. How good our data is: how sure, how recent, and whether the price was checked.
4. Price: the monthly price of the cheapest plan that fits. A free plan counts too.
5. Ease: a tool that does several steps counts in the "Fewest tools" choice, and a little in "Recommended".

On a feature's page, tools with this as their main feature come first. After that it's about how sure and how recent our data is, and then the lowest price. In All tools you choose the order yourself: best match, name, price or last checked.
methodology.moneyBody: Partner links and paid spots don't count for the order. The code that decides the order cannot even read the data about money. Every change runs a test that compares the results with and without partner links: they must be exactly the same. Paid spots always have the label "Sponsored" and are kept apart from the results.
methodology.statusVerified: We saw it word for word on the maker's official site, and we are very sure about it.
methodology.statusSupported: There is a source: several separate sources say the same, or the official site mentions it. We haven't seen it word for word yet.
methodology.statusCommunity: Based only on what users say online, such as on forums and social media.
methodology.statusUnverified: One other website, or a guess by our editors. We still need to check it.
methodology.confidenceBody: We work this number out from the evidence. It is not a feeling. It depends on five things: the type of source (the official site counts most), whether the sentence really is on the page word for word, how old the observation is, how we checked it (an automatic check counts more than searching online) and how many separate sources say the same. Does a check fail, for example an impossible price jump? Then the number stays low. An AI may never say for itself how sure it is: that doesn't count as evidence.
methodology.freshnessBody: Every kind of data stays good for a while only. When that time is over, you see "This information may be outdated" with the date of the last check. These are the time limits now:
methodology.freshnessRow: {kind}: fresh up to {fresh} days, may be outdated after {aging} days
methodology.agentsBody: Our software checks official pricing pages, update logs and websites. It also finds new tools. We only put a new price online after we saw the same price twice, some time apart. Big price jumps, tools that stop without an official message and new tools are looked at by a person first. Does the software suddenly see very many changes? Then publishing stops by itself. We write down every automatic change, and we can undo it.
methodology.aiBody: We use AI to understand your question when searching for words isn't enough. And to get data from official pages. Then we always check that every value really is in the source, word for word. Text made with AI gets a label. The advice itself is worked out by us; no AI writes it.
methodology.limitsBody: Prices are as the maker shows them: usually without VAT, and sometimes different per country. We convert dollar amounts with the ECB rate of that day. That is an estimate. Part of the data comes from other websites. That data has the status Sourced until our software has seen it on the official site.
methodology.correctionsBody: Something wrong? Report it, with a source. We respond, and you can read all corrections in public.

disclosureInfo.intro: AIToolsWijzer is free. We do make money, but it may never change our advice. Here's how:
disclosureInfo.affiliateBody: For some tools we get money (a commission) if you take a paid subscription through our link. Such a link has the label "partner link", and rel="sponsored" in the code. You pay nothing extra. The order and our advice stay the same, with or without a link. We test that automatically.
disclosureInfo.clicksTitle: What we track when you click
disclosureInfo.clicksBody: Links to other sites go through /go/. That shows us which pages are useful. We keep nothing about you: no cookies, only a code that changes every day and cannot be traced back.
disclosureInfo.sponsoredBody: Paid spots always have the label "Sponsored" and look different. They are never placed among the normal results.
disclosureInfo.never1: Take money for a higher spot, or for being in our list.
disclosureInfo.never3: Leave out tools because we earn nothing from them.

about.title: About AIToolsWijzer
about.metaDescription: AIToolsWijzer helps you find the right AI tools for what you want to do. With sources, and nobody can pay for a better spot.
about.intro: AIToolsWijzer answers one question: I want to do something, which AI tool fits? You get advice with prices, sources and alternatives.
about.howBody: A small team of editors and software that checks official sources automatically. People decide on new tools, big changes and corrections. The software does the routine work, and we write down every automatic action.
about.contactFallback: Spotted a mistake? Report it with the form. A business question? Use the form on Check your tools.
about.logosBody: Some tools show their logo. The logo belongs to the company that makes the tool. We only use it so you can spot the tool quickly. The logos come from Simple Icons and are stored on our own server. If a company wants its logo removed, it can send us a message through Corrections.

privacy.title: Privacy and cookies
privacy.metaDescription: What AIToolsWijzer does with data: counting visits without cookies, no tracking, and e-mail only when you confirm twice.
privacy.intro: Short version: we don't track you with cookies and we don't sell data. Below is exactly what we do with your data, why and for how long.

analytics.title: Visit statistics (without cookies)
analytics.body: We count page visits on our server. For that we make a code from your IP address and browser version every day. The code cannot be traced back, and the secret key changes every day. We don't store your IP address itself. We cannot link visits on different days to each other. Legal basis: legitimate interest (we want to see how the site is used).

match.title: Questions you ask
match.body: What you type as a question is stored to make the site better. We remove e-mail addresses, phone numbers, links and long numbers first. We keep it for 90 days. Do we use AI (a language model) to understand your question? Then your question goes to our AI provider (Anthropic). It only uses it to give the answer.

cookie.title: One cookie that is needed
cookie.body: If you save a receipt, we set the cookie "aitw_my". That way you find your receipts on this device again. The cookie is needed for what you ask for yourself. There are no other cookies. We keep it for 12 months.

email.title: E-mail (newsletter and alerts)
email.body: Only if you confirm your sign-up twice. We store your e-mail address, your language, the text you agreed to and when. You can unsubscribe with one click in every e-mail. We then delete your alerts. We send e-mail through our e-mail company. Sign-ups you don't confirm are deleted after 30 days. Copies of sent e-mails are kept for 90 days, to fix delivery problems.

leads.title: Advice requests
leads.body: Do you ask for advice? Then we store your name, e-mail, company and message, so we can get in touch. We keep this for 24 months after the last contact.

video.title: Videos
video.body: Videos only load from YouTube (in privacy-enhanced mode) when you press play.
video.api: We get video lists and titles from YouTube, through the public channel feeds or through the YouTube API Services. YouTube content is subject to the YouTube Terms of Service and the Google Privacy Policy.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You may ask which data we have about you, and ask us to correct or delete it. You may also object. E-mail us at the address below. You can also complain to your data protection authority (in the Netherlands: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens).

bot.title: About AIToolsWijzerBot
bot.metaDescription: What our crawler fetches, how often, and how to block it.
bot.intro: AIToolsWijzerBot keeps the prices and facts on AIToolsWijzer up to date. It only reads public pages of the AI tools we list, so we can cite them as sources.
bot.what1: Official pricing pages, to check the prices we show.
bot.what2: Home pages, to check that a tool is still online (a light request that reads at most 16 KB).
bot.what3: Official changelogs and RSS/Atom feeds, for release notes.
bot.what4: Public pages of new candidate tools, before a person reviews them.
bot.how1: It follows robots.txt for the user agent AIToolsWijzerBot (re-read at least once a day).
bot.how2: At least 5 seconds between requests to the same site, and at most 2 at a time.
bot.how3: Pricing pages at most about once a day; home pages and feeds about every 6 hours.
bot.how4: No logins, no forms, no cookies and no JavaScript. It only reads.
bot.storeBody: A fingerprint (hash) of the page to notice changes, and at most a short quote with a link to the source, shown next to the fact it supports. We never republish your pages.
bot.blockBody: Add this to your robots.txt. We pick it up within 24 hours:
bot.contactCorrections: Or report an error on the corrections page.

static.failed: This could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
static.needsJs: This feature works in your browser. For that, JavaScript must be on.
static.correctionsIntro: Is something wrong? Report the tool, what is wrong and a link to the source. We check it on the official page.
static.privacyHosting: This site is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub processes technical data, such as your IP address, to show the pages and prevent abuse (see GitHub's privacy statement). We do not count visits and set no cookies.
static.privacyBrowserTitle: Your question and Check your tools
static.privacyBrowser: Your question and Check your tools are worked out entirely in your browser. What you enter is not sent to us and not stored.
static.disclosureClicks: Links to tools go through a redirect page straight to the tool's website. We do not count clicks.
static.apiTermsBody: Use is free with attribution and a link to the relevant AIToolsWijzer page. The API consists of static JSON files that are rebuilt whenever the data changes. No guarantee of accuracy or availability; always check important decisions at the source.

reason.too_many_status_changes: Too many status changes in one run; frozen to be safe.

reason.same_name: Two tools share the same name.

reason.monthly_audit: Judge a random sample of automated decisions; this keeps autonomy honest.
reason.dependency: An integration the system relies on is failing.
reason.login_failures: Many failed admin logins in a short time: possibly a password-guessing attack. Logins are rate-limited; consider changing passwords and checking the audit log.
reason.vendor_correction: The maker of this tool reports an error. Check the source and update the data if it holds up.
reason.user_correction: A visitor reports an error with a source. Check it and update the data if it holds up.

agentDescription.health: Checks every dependency (database, agents, e-mail, keys, legal details, backups) and escalates failures.
agentDescription.escalation: Applies safe defaults after deadlines, closes items whose cause has cleared, pauses failing agents and keeps your inbox within budget.

agentDescription.fx: Loads the daily ECB euro reference rates.
agentDescription.pricing: Checks official pricing pages; confirms prices and publishes confirmed changes.
agentDescription.broken-link: Checks tool websites; marks tools unreachable after repeated failures and restores them automatically.
agentDescription.change-detection: Reads official changelogs and feeds and publishes new releases to Pulse.
agentDescription.social: Tracks GitHub stars and releases and Hacker News mentions (public APIs only).
agentDescription.video: Adds official channel uploads, optionally finds tutorials and reviews, and removes videos that disappeared.
agentDescription.discovery: Collects candidate AI tools from Show HN and GitHub; publishes nothing.
agentDescription.verification: Checks candidates (reachability, AI relevance, blocklist, duplicates, pricing, legal pages) and hands good ones to you.
agentDescription.duplicate: Flags tools that share a website or a name; merging stays your decision.
agentDescription.monetization: Checks affiliate links weekly; falls back to the direct link when one breaks.
agentDescription.recommendation: Runs the golden set of real use cases every night and escalates regressions.
agentDescription.opportunity: Ranks affiliate, content and readiness opportunities by expected value; tunes the LLM threshold within your limits.
agentDescription.content: Optional (LLM): drafts texts for new draft tools and translates tool texts into extra languages.
agentDescription.reporter: Builds the weekly report and e-mails it to you when e-mail is configured.
agentDescription.audit: Monthly random sample of automated decisions for you to judge; measures precision per confidence band.
agentDescription.news: Reads media feeds (RSS and YouTube) every hour and publishes AI news: headline, outlet and link, never the article text.
agentDescription.new-tools: Every morning around 07:00: puts the most popular new tools that pass every hard gate again online in quarantine (at most the daily number you set), and takes tools out of quarantine after 7 green days. More than 25 in 24 hours: publishes nothing and asks you.
